Threshold value 1: This value should make sure that the sky is not black, or has any black pixels

Threshold value 2: This value should make sure that the mountains in the distance are visible, even if the sky turns blackish

#create image segmentation func
def image_segmentation(img, threshold):
  #apply threshold
  _, binary_img = cv2.threshold(img, threshold, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY)
  return binary_img

#First image should make sure the sky has no black pixels
threshold = 100
binary_img1 = image_segmentation(cactus_img, threshold)
#plot original img and first threshold next to each other
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(cactus_img, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Original Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(binary_img1, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Binary Image Threshold 1')
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()

#Second image makes sure that the mountains are visible even if the sky is a little black
threshold = 175
binary_img2 = image_segmentation(cactus_img, threshold)
#plot original img and second threshold next to each other
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(cactus_img, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Original Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(binary_img2, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Binary Image Threshold 2')
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()

Thresholds picked¶

  • Threshold one = 100
  • Threshold two = 175

In [3]:
#load gaussian noise image
gaussian_noise_img = cv2.imread('gaussian noise.png')


#remove noise using gaussian method defined in lesson

#create function similar to module to add noise to the img
def add_gaussian_noise(img, mean, std_dev):
    h, w, c = img.shape
    noise = np.random.normal(mean, std_dev, (h,w,c))
    # Convert image to float32 for addition
    img_float = img.astype(np.float32)
    # Add noise to the float image
    noisy_img_float = cv2.add(img_float, noise.astype(np.float32))
    # Clip values to be within the valid range [0, 255] before converting back to uint8
    noisy_img = np.clip(noisy_img_float, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return noisy_img
#define guassian blur function
def gaussian_blur(img, kernel_size):
    blurred_img = cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (kernel_size, kernel_size), 0)
    return blurred_img
#add guassian noise to img
noisy_img = add_gaussian_noise(gaussian_noise_img, 0, 25)
#apply blur
blurred_img = gaussian_blur(noisy_img, 5)

#apply median filter. Define function to use OpenCV median filter
def median_filter(img, kernel_size):
    filtered_img = cv2.medianBlur(img, kernel_size)
    return filtered_img

#apply median filter
filtered_img = median_filter(gaussian_noise_img, 5)

#plot original img, gaussian img, and median img
plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.imshow(gaussian_noise_img, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Original Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
plt.imshow(blurred_img, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Gaussian Blur Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.imshow(filtered_img, cmap='gray')
plt.title('Median Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()

What did I learn about the median filter¶

I learned that it is very similar to the Gaussian Blur function taught in the lesson but in this case, it actually produced a much cleaner result. Not sure if I did something wrong here but it looks much better¶

#load the peppers png
peppers_img = cv2.imread('peppers.png')
peppers_img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(peppers_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

#perform RGB histogram equalization to img
channels = cv2.split(peppers_img_rgb)
equalized_channels = []
for channel in channels:
    equalized_channels.append(cv2.equalizeHist(channel))
equalized_rgb = cv2.merge(equalized_channels)

#plot original and new picture
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(peppers_img_rgb)
plt.title('Original Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(equalized_rgb)
plt.title('Equalized Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()

channels = cv2.split(peppers_img_rgb)

for i, channel in enumerate(channels):

    else:

#load the coins png
coins_img = cv2.imread('coins.png')

#create watershed alg similar to one in module
def watershed_segmentation(img):
    # Convert the image to grayscale
    gray_image = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    #apply gaussian blur
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(gray_image, (5, 5), 0)
    # Apply thresholding
    _, thresholded = cv2.threshold(blurred, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
    # Morphological operations
    kernel = np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)
    opening = cv2.morphologyEx(thresholded, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel, iterations=3)
    #Sure background
    sure_bg = cv2.dilate(opening, kernel, iterations=3)
    #Sure foreground
    dist_transform = cv2.distanceTransform(opening, cv2.DIST_L2, 5)
    _, sure_fg = cv2.threshold(dist_transform, 0.5 * dist_transform.max(), 255, 0)
    #Unknown region
    sure_fg = np.uint8(sure_fg)
    unknown = cv2.subtract(sure_bg, sure_fg)
    # Marker labelling
    _, markers = cv2.connectedComponents(sure_fg)
    # Add one to all labels so that sure background is not 0, but 1
    markers = markers + 1
    # Now, mark the region of unknown with zero
    markers[unknown == 255] = 0
    # Apply watershed
    result = img.copy()
    cv2.watershed(result, markers)
    result[markers == -1] = [0, 255,0]
    return result
#Apply watershed to coins image
segmented_coins = watershed_segmentation(coins_img)
#plot original and segmented next to each other
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(cv2.cvtColor(coins_img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
plt.title('Original Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(cv2.cvtColor(segmented_coins, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
plt.title('Segmented Image')
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()
